components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.fact: 明 (built from 日 'sun' plus 月 'moon' — the two brightest things in the sky, together meaning 'bright') combines with 天 ('day') to give 明天 a still-visible logic: 'the bright/next day,' the same 明+[time word] pattern behind 明年 ('next year').

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān nǐ yǒu kòng ma?
examples.english: Are you free tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn jiàn.
examples.english: Let's meet at eight tomorrow morning.

components.note: 立 (stand) — the person-standing radical, as in 站 itself and 位 position; here it carries the meaning of standing.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound exactly: 站 zhàn, also in 战 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.fact: 站 means 'to stand' and a place where vehicles stop: 车站 'station', 火车站, 公交站 'bus stop', 网站 'website'. 站住！ is a command meaning 'Stop!'

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhàn zài zhè tiáo xiàn hòumiàn.
examples.english: Please stand behind this line.

examples.pinyin: Xià yí zhàn shì Rénmín Guǎngchǎng.
examples.english: The next stop is People's Square.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.
束 (bind) — a 木 tied around with a cord 口: a bundle of wood. 束 also gives 速 sù (hurried) and 嗽 sòu.

example.fact: 结束 pairs two separate images of closure — 结 ('to knot,' from the thread radical 纟) and 束 (a bundle of wood bound with rope) — into a compound that reads almost literally as 'tied up and bundled,' i.e. wrapped up and finished.

examples.pinyin: Huìyì shénme shíhou jiéshù?
examples.english: When does the meeting end?

examples.hanzi: 学期结束以后,我要去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Xuéqī jiéshù yǐhòu, wǒ yào qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: After the semester ends, I'm going traveling.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
司 (sī) is a sound clue for 词 cí and 饲 sì; as a word it means to manage, as in 公司 company.

example.hanzi: 我在一家外国公司工作。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài yì jiā wàiguó gōngsī gōngzuò.
example.english: I work at a foreign company.
example.fact: 公司 pairs 公 ('public, shared') with 司 ('to manage, to take charge of') — literally 'a publicly-run undertaking,' a fitting label for the modern idea of a jointly-owned commercial enterprise.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de gōngsī lí jiā hěn jìn.
examples.english: My company is close to home.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī míngtiān zhāo rén.
examples.english: This company is hiring tomorrow.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.pinyin: Tā chéngwéi le yì míng yīshēng.
example.fact: 成为 is reserved for becoming a noun or role ('成为医生,' 'become a doctor') — for becoming an adjective or state, Chinese switches to 变得 ('变得更好,' 'become better'), a split English's single word 'become' doesn't make.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéngwéi yì míng lǎoshī.
examples.english: He wants to become a teacher.

examples.pinyin: Shuǐ chéngwéile bīng.
examples.english: The water turned into ice.

components.note: 水 (water) — water and flow: 永 first meant a long river. 泳 yǒng (swimming) added the water radical later.
辶 (walk) — movement and distance, as in 过, 近, 进: 远 is a road that goes far.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuǎn; 元 also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.fact: 远 (built on the 'walking' radical 辶, evoking a long road) contributes 'far, distant' — paired with 永 ('perpetual'), 永远 projects that image of physical distance onto time, arriving at 'forever.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒngyuǎn shì péngyou.
examples.english: We'll be friends forever.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒngyuǎn bú huì fàngqì.
examples.english: He will never give up.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.fact: 帮助 doubles up two independently meaningful roots for 'help' — 帮 (from 邦 'a state, nation' plus 巾 'a banner,' picturing a flag people rally around) and 助 (力 'strength' lent to someone) — the same synonym-compounding strategy behind words like 喜欢 and 应该.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bāngzhù wǒ xuéxí Zhōngwén.
examples.english: The teacher helps me study Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 这本书对学生很有帮助。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì xuésheng hěn yǒu bāngzhù.
examples.english: This book is very helpful to students.

meanings: (after 对/就 + a noun or pronoun) as far as ... is concerned

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 对我来说,这是一个很难的决定。
example.pinyin: Duì wǒ láishuō, zhè shì yí gè hěn nán de juédìng.
example.english: As far as I'm concerned, this is a difficult decision.
example.fact: 来说 never stands alone — it is the back half of the fixed frame 对/就 + [topic] + 来说 ("as far as X is concerned"), one of Mandarin's most common ways to frame a personal viewpoint before stating a claim, roughly matching English "-wise" or "in terms of."

examples.hanzi: 对学生来说,考试很重要。
examples.pinyin: Duì xuésheng lái shuō, kǎoshì hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: For students, exams are important.

examples.hanzi: 一般来说,他八点到公司。
examples.pinyin: Yìbān lái shuō, tā bā diǎn dào gōngsī.
examples.english: Generally speaking, he gets to the office at eight.

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.

example.fact: 多少 and 几 both ask 'how many/how much,' but 几 expects a small, countable answer under about ten (几个人, 'a handful of people'), while 多少 carries no such ceiling — a scope distinction English's single question 'how many' doesn't mark.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu duōshao ge péngyou?
examples.english: How many friends do you have?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào hái shèng duōshao.
examples.english: I don't know how much is left.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 哇 is an exclamation of surprise, wow.
圭 (guī) — loose sound hint (wā vs guī); same part in 挂 guà and 娃 wá.

example.fact: 哇 shows amazement, as in 'wow'. Doubled as 哇哇 it imitates a baby's crying. After u or ao the particle 啊 may become 哇: 好哇 (hǎo wa).

examples.pinyin: Wā, nǐ de xīn chē zhēn piàoliang!
examples.english: Wow, your new car is gorgeous!

examples.pinyin: Wā, zhège dàngāo tài dà le!
examples.english: Wow, this cake is huge!

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.fact: 名字 is a full name: 名 'given name', 姓 'family name'. 名 also means 'fame' (出名 'famous') and ranks (第一名 'first place'). In formal counting it is a measure word for people: 三名学生.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiěxià nǐ de míngzi.
examples.english: Please write down your name.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bān yǒu sānshí míng xuésheng.
examples.english: This class has thirty students.

components.note: 它 (it) — an old picture of a snake; 蛇 shé (snake) adds 虫. Its pronoun use is borrowed. Sound series: 拖 tuō, 驼 tuó.
亻 (person) — marks words about people, as in 你 you, 他 he, 做 do. Here it shows 们 pluralises person words (我们, 他们).
门 (mén) gives the sound: 们 is men (neutral tone), the same syllable as 门 gate.

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē māo, tāmen dōu hěn kě'ài.
example.english: These cats — they're all very cute.
example.fact: Mandarin's third-person plural quietly splits by referent — 他们 for people or mixed groups, 她们 for all-female groups, 它们 for animals or things — even though all three are pronounced identically, tāmen; the distinction exists only in writing.

examples.hanzi: 我有两只小狗,它们很听话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu liǎng zhī xiǎo gǒu, tāmen hěn tīnghuà.
examples.english: I have two puppies and they're very obedient.

examples.pinyin: Huā kāi le, tāmen zhēn piàoliang.
examples.english: The flowers have bloomed; they're so pretty.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.

example.fact: 总是 means 'always' (habitual and a bit critical). 总共 is 'in total', 总统 'president', and 总会 means 'surely will eventually': 总会好的 'it will be fine in the end'. The simplified form is 總.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì xiàozhe shuōhuà.
examples.english: He always speaks with a smile.

examples.pinyin: Zǒnggòng yǒu duōshao ge rén?
examples.english: How many people are there in total?

components.note: 石 (stone) — stone and hardness, as in 碎 shatter, 破 break, 码 code: 确 is solid, certain.
角 (jiǎo) replaces 隺 (hè) of 確 and is only a loose clue for què.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.pinyin: Nǐ quèdìng yào zǒu zhè tiáo lù ma?
example.english: Are you sure you want to take this road?
example.fact: 确定 slides between adjective ("certain, sure") and verb ("to confirm, to fix") depending on context — 你确定吗? asks "are you sure?," while 确定时间 means "to fix the time" — one word covering two different English parts of speech.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú quèdìng tā zài bu zài jiā.
examples.english: I'm not sure whether he's home.

examples.pinyin: Huìyì shíjiān yǐjīng quèdìng le.
examples.english: The meeting time has been confirmed.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.pinyin: Mén wài yǒurén zài děng nǐ.
example.english: There's someone waiting for you outside the door.
example.fact: 有人 doubles as the standard sign for an occupied public restroom, the mirror opposite of 没人 ("vacant, no one") — a practical, everyday use of the phrase well beyond its literal meaning "there is a person."

examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén qiāo mén, nǐ qù kànkan.
examples.english: Someone's knocking; go take a look.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ yǒu rén ma?
examples.english: Is anyone here?

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
木 (tree) — doubled as 林 on top: a thorny shrub, the original 'bramble'. The wood family appears in 树, 桥. 'Pain' (痛楚) comes from the thorns.
疋 (shū) — the bottom part; the sound clue is only loose today (chǔ vs shū).

example.fact: 清楚 attaches after a verb as a resultative complement marking that the action was carried out to a clear, thorough degree — 说清楚 ('explain clearly'), 想清楚 ('think it through') — filling the same grammatical slot as 完 ('finish') or 好 ('well') after other verbs.

examples.pinyin: Zhège zì wǒ kàn bu qīngchu.
examples.english: I can't see this character clearly.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shìqing shuō de hěn qīngchu.
examples.english: He explained things very clearly.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.english: Let's have dinner together in the evening.
example.fact: 晚 is built from 日 ('sun') plus 免, traditionally read as the sun 'slipping away' — giving 晚 its sense of lateness, the same root behind 晚安 ('good night') and 晚点 ('running late').

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang yǒu yǔ.
examples.english: It will rain tonight.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang shí diǎn shuìjiào.
examples.english: He goes to bed at ten every night.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.

example.english: Pay attention to safety when driving.
example.fact: 安 (a woman 女 sheltered under a roof 宀, an image of domestic peace) contributes 'at ease, secure,' while 全 (a treasure 玉 kept whole and undamaged) contributes 'complete, intact' — together painting safety as being both protected and unharmed.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfang hěn ānquán.
examples.english: This place is very safe.

examples.pinyin: Háizi de ānquán zuì zhòngyào.
examples.english: Children's safety is the most important.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thought, as in 想 think, 思 ponder, 急 anxious; in 怎 it is only loosely linked to the question sense.
乍 (zhà) is a loose sound clue for zěn; 乍 also sounds out 作 zuò, 昨 zuó and 炸 zhà.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌 table, 板 board; 样 once meant a tree (acorn) and later "form, pattern".
羊 (yáng, sheep) is a near-exact sound clue for yàng; 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 养 yǎng.

example.fact: 怎样 and its slightly longer cousin 怎么样 are near-interchangeable ways to ask "how/what's it like" — native speakers swap freely between them, though 怎么样 dominates casual speech while 怎样 reads a touch more formal or literary.

examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài zěnyàng zuò?
examples.english: How do you make this dish?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ juéde tā zěnyàng?
examples.english: What do you think of him?

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
十 (shí, ten) is a loose sound clue for 什 (shén, shí in 什锦); old sense "a set of ten", hence "assorted". In 什么 it is simply "what".
幺 (tiny, a thread) — 么 looks like 幺 and was borrowed as a simplified form for the light particle in 什么, 怎么, 这么. The shape does not explain the meaning today.
厶 (loop) — the visible lower part, a small curl. Memory aid: a tiny stroke 丿 over a curl — a 'little something' you ask about: 什么 what?

example.fact: 没什么, taken apart, literally says "doesn't have what" (没 "not have" + 什么 "what") — from there it drifted into a fixed conversational reflex for waving off an apology or thanks, the same kind of semantic bleaching English's "it's nothing" has gone through.

examples.pinyin: "Xièxie nǐ!" "Méi shénme, xiǎoshì."
examples.english: "Thank you!" "It's nothing, a small matter."

examples.hanzi: 你怎么了?没什么,我只是累了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme le? Méi shénme, wǒ zhǐshì lèi le.
examples.english: What's wrong? Nothing, I'm just tired.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a lump of earth; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
夬 (guài) is a loose clue; 快 kuài shares it and sounds exactly like 块.

example.english: I'd like a piece of cake.
example.fact: 块 counts lumps and pieces (一块肉, 一块蛋糕). In speech it also means 'yuan': 五块钱 'five yuan'. 一块儿 means 'together'. It is a casual alternative to written 元.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dàngāo hěn tián.
examples.english: This piece of cake is very sweet.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū èrshí kuài qián.
examples.english: This book costs twenty yuan.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.english: I go home at six every day.
example.fact: 回家 fuses the directional verb 回 ('to return') straight onto its destination 家 ('home') with no preposition in between — Chinese verb-object compounds like this routinely skip the 'to' that English inserts before a destination.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huíjiā shuìjiào.
examples.english: I want to go home and sleep.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò nǐ huíjiā ma?
examples.english: Are you going home this weekend?

components.note: 留 (liú) is a sound clue for 溜 liū, 榴 liú and 瘤 liú; as a word it means to stay or keep.

example.pinyin: Qǐng liúxià nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ.
example.fact: 留 is 'stay behind' or 'leave behind': 留下, 留言 'leave a message', 留学 'study abroad', 留意 'pay attention'. It can also mean 'keep': 留着 'save it'.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ liúxià míngzi.
examples.english: Please leave your name here.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ liú xiàlái chī wǎnfàn ba.
examples.english: Stay for dinner.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.

example.fact: 周 is a written, modern way to say 'week': 周一 'Monday', 周末 'weekend', 下周 'next week'. It also means 'around': 周围 'surroundings'. It is a very common surname Zhōu as well.

examples.hanzi: 这周我很忙，周日也要上班。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhōu wǒ hěn máng, zhōurì yě yào shàngbān.
examples.english: I am busy this week, even working on Sunday.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù páshān ba.
examples.english: Let's go hiking this weekend.

components.note: 心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.fact: 愿意 is built on the heart radical 心 in 愿, marking it as willingness that comes from one's own desire — distinct from 可以 ('is permitted to') or 能 ('is able to'), 愿意 is specifically about consent, not permission or capability.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú yuànyì qù nàlǐ.
examples.english: I'm not willing to go there.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yuànyì hé wǒ yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.english: Would you like to go with me?

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.
刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 划 is to cut a line, then to plan (计划) or row (huá).

example.hanzi: 我们的旅行计划改变了。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de lǚxíng jìhuà gǎibiàn le.
example.fact: 计 (built on the speech radical 讠 plus 十, since counting was once reckoned aloud) contributes 'to calculate, to reckon,' while 划 contributes 'to delineate, to map out' — together giving 计划 its literal sense of 'to reckon and lay out.'

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme jìhuà ma?
examples.english: Do you have any plans?

examples.pinyin: Tā jìhuà míngnián qù Rìběn.
examples.english: He plans to go to Japan next year.

components.note: 父 (father) — a father-word radical, as in 爷 grandpa; 爸 is dad.
巴 (bā) is a close sound clue for bà; 巴 also sounds out 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 爸 bà.

example.fact: 爸 is usually doubled as 爸爸 in speech. The formal word is 父亲. Like 妈妈, 爸爸 resembles baby words for parents in many languages, because the sounds ba and ma are among babies' first.

examples.pinyin: Bà, nǐ zài zuò shénme?
examples.english: Dad, what are you doing?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàmā jīntiān lái kàn wǒ.
examples.english: My parents are coming to see me today.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people; 俩 is two people, as in 咱俩 the two of us.
两 (liǎng, two) — same sound family: 俩 liǎ is a contraction of 两个 two people.

example.english: The two of us are good friends.
example.fact: 俩 comes after a pronoun to mean 'both of': 咱俩, 你们俩, 他们俩. It already includes the number two, so it takes no measure word. It is colloquial, with a contracted 两个. Read liǎng it means 'trick', as in 伎俩.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen liǎ shì tóngshì.
examples.english: The two of them are colleagues.

examples.pinyin: Zánmen liǎ yìqǐ qù ba.
examples.english: The two of us should go together.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.

example.english: The car is parked at the door.
example.fact: 停 means 'stop' and 'park': 停车 'park a car', 停电 'power cut', 暂停 'pause'. The thing stops moving, which is different from 站, where someone stands. 别停！ means 'Don't stop!'

examples.pinyin: Yǔ hái méiyǒu tíng.
examples.english: The rain hasn't stopped yet.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù néng tíngchē.
examples.english: You can't park here.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".

example.fact: Chinese runs three separate "can'ts" alongside its three "can's" — 可以 (permission), 会 (learned skill), 能 (ability/circumstance) — so 不可以 means "not allowed," 不会 means "don't know how," and 不能 means "not able to right now," each negating a different flavor of "can."

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù néng tíngchē.
examples.english: You can't park here.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān bù néng lái shàngkè.
examples.english: He can't come to class today.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 她, 姐, 奶; 妈 is mother.
马 (mǎ) is a close sound clue for mā; also in 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
白 (white, bright) — 的 first meant bright and clear, as in 的确 dí què.
勺 (sháo) is a loose sound clue for dì; 勺 also sounds out 约 yuē and 钓 diào.

example.fact: 他妈的 is one of Mandarin's most common curse interjections, built literally from "his mother's" (他 "his" + 妈 "mother" + 的, the possessive particle) — an ellipsis of a much cruder insult about someone's mother, worn down by generations of casual use into a general-purpose expletive closer in force to English "damn it" than to its literal, far more offensive roots.

examples.hanzi: 你不要说他妈的,这样不礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào shuō tā mā de, zhèyàng bù lǐmào.
examples.english: Don't say "damn", it's impolite.

examples.hanzi: 老师说他妈的是一句脏话。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī shuō tā mā de shì yí jù zānghuà.
examples.english: The teacher said "damn it" is a swear word.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 话 is speech.
舌 (shé, tongue) fits the meaning (speaking) and is a loose sound clue for huà; also in 活 huó.

example.fact: 说话 is a verb-object compound that literally means 'to speak speech' — 话 already means 'words, speech' on its own, so the verb 说 ('to say') takes its own near-synonym as a built-in object, letting 说话 function as a self-contained verb for 'to talk.'

examples.pinyin: Qǐng màn yìdiǎn shuōhuà.
examples.english: Please speak a bit slower.

examples.hanzi: 图书馆里不能大声说话。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ bù néng dàshēng shuōhuà.
examples.english: You can't talk loudly in the library.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth/speech family, as in 吃, 叫, 问. Memory aid: set things apart by calling them out with the mouth — 另外 besides.
力 (strength) — the bottom. No reliable etymology. Memory aid: strength to pull one piece apart from the rest — 'another, separate'.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì lìng yí jiàn shì.
example.fact: 另 is 'another' or 'separately': 另一个 'another one', 另外 'in addition'. It is more formal than 别的 or 其他. Don't confuse 另 (lìng) with 别 (bié), which contains it.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ lìngwài mǎile yìxiē shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: I bought some extra fruit.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de lìng yì zhī shǒutào ne?
examples.english: Where's your other glove?

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xīn tiào de hěn kuài.
example.fact: In Chinese thinking and feeling live in the heart: 开心 'happy', 小心 'careful', 担心 'worry', 放心 'relax'. Characters about thought and emotion carry 心 or 忄, such as 想 and 快.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié dānxīn, wǒ méi shì.
examples.english: Don't worry, I'm fine.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn xìxīn de rén.
examples.english: She is a very careful person.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.

example.pinyin: Tā sòng wǒ yì duǒ huā.
example.fact: 花 means 'flower' (measure word 朵) and also 'to spend': 花钱 'spend money', 花时间 'spend time'. It also means 'fancy, patterned': 花衣服 'patterned clothes'.

examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu hěn duō huā.
examples.english: There are many flowers in the yard.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huāle liǎng ge xiǎoshí zuòfàn.
examples.english: I spent two hours cooking.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 好, 姐; 她 is the female "she", coined to parallel 他.
也 (yě) is only a loose sound clue for tā; the 他 pair is the same part.
亻 (person) — marks words about people, as in 你 you, 他 he, 做 do. Here it shows 们 pluralises person words (我们, 他们).
门 (mén) gives the sound: 们 is men (neutral tone), the same syllable as 门 gate.

example.pinyin: Tāmen shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
example.fact: 她 didn't exist before the early 20th century — Chinese had no gendered third-person pronoun until 女 was added to the existing pronoun 也/他 to coin a dedicated character for "she," under pressure from translating Western literature; 她们 is simply the plural built on that comparatively young character.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen míngtiān qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: They (the women) are going on a trip tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan tāmen chàng de gē.
examples.english: I really like the songs they (the women) sing.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.hanzi: 有些人不喜欢辣的食物。
example.pinyin: Yǒuxiē rén bù xǐhuan là de shíwù.
example.english: Some people don't like spicy food.
example.fact: 有些 can modify a noun ("有些人," "some people") or slide in front of an adjective to soften it into "somewhat, rather" ("有些累," "rather tired") — the same dual noun-quantifier/degree-adverb behavior shared by its near-synonym 一些.

examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē cài tài xián le.
examples.english: Some of the dishes are too salty.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒuxiē lèi.
examples.english: I'm a bit tired today.

components.note: 门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.fact: 门 is also the measure word for school subjects and courses (一门课, 'one course') and for cannons, which surprises learners who know it only as 'door'. It forms many compounds for entrances, like 大门 (main gate) and 门口 (doorway).

examples.pinyin: Ménkǒu yǒu yí ge rén zài děng nǐ.
examples.english: Someone is waiting for you at the door.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ chūqù de shíhou guānmén.
examples.english: Please close the door when you go out.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
讠 (speech) — words, as in 说, 请, 诉: you thank someone with words.
射 (shè) is a loose sound clue for xiè; in 谢谢 the tone drops to neutral on the second.

example.pinyin: Wǒ fēicháng gǎnxiè nǐ de bāngzhù.
example.english: I'm very grateful for your help.
example.fact: 感谢 sits a register above the everyday, reduplicated 谢谢 — reserved for more sincere or formal gratitude (speeches, thank-you letters, public acknowledgments), while 谢谢 handles the reflexive "thanks" of daily conversation.

examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè dàjiā de zhīchí.
examples.english: Thank you all for your support.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn gǎnxiè lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen.
examples.english: I'm very grateful to the teacher for teaching us.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.

example.fact: 谈谈 reduplicates the verb 谈 ('to talk, converse') into a softer, more casual invitation — the same tone-softening reduplication behind 看看 ('take a look') and 谢谢 itself, where doubling a single-syllable verb makes the action feel brief and low-pressure.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé nǐ tántan.
examples.english: I'd like to talk with you.

examples.pinyin: Nǐmen zuò xiàlai tántan ba.
examples.english: Why don't you sit down and have a chat.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.english: We have settled on a time.
example.fact: 定 often works as a resultative or fixed-in-place idea: 定下来 means to settle down or be decided, and 定 can book things in the sense of 'fix' a room or seat (定位子). Do not confuse it with 订 (dìng, to order or book), which is the usual character for reservations.

examples.hanzi: 我们已经定了会议时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐjīng dìngle huìyì shíjiān.
examples.english: We've already set the time for the meeting.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yídìng huì zhǔnshí dào.
examples.english: I will definitely arrive on time.

components.note: 于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.fact: 于 is a formal, written preposition that covers 'in', 'at', 'to', 'from' and even 'than' depending on the verb, so it shows up in set patterns like 生于 (born in), 关于 (about) and 对于 (regarding). Everyday speech usually prefers 在, 到 or 比 instead.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī wèiyú shìzhōngxīn.
examples.english: This company is located downtown.

examples.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì gāo yú píngjūnfēn.
examples.english: His grades are above average.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.english: Let's keep in touch more from now on.
example.fact: 以后 can attach after a time word or clause to mean "after X" (毕业以后, "after graduating"), or stand alone at the front of a sentence meaning simply "from now on" — two distinct grammatical slots for one word, told apart only by whether anything precedes it.

examples.pinyin: Yǐhòu nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do you want to do in the future?

examples.pinyin: Bìyè yǐhòu, tā qùle Shànghǎi.
examples.english: After graduating, he went to Shanghai.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ bié guǎn.
example.english: Don't get involved in this matter.
example.fact: 管 also means 'pipe or tube', and the sense of 'to manage' grew from it. A very common phrase is 不管 ('no matter, regardless'), and 管 on its own can mean 'to meddle in' or 'to take responsibility for', as in 别管我 ('leave me alone').

examples.pinyin: Nǐ guǎn de tài duō le, bié shēngqì.
examples.english: You're meddling too much, don't be mad.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī guǎn cáiwù.
examples.english: He takes care of finances at the company.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen de jiéhūn zhàopiàn.
example.fact: 照 (built on the fire/light radical 灬, since photography is literally light striking a surface) contributes 'to shine, to capture light,' and 片 contributes 'a thin, flat piece' — together 照片 reads almost like 'a piece with light captured on it,' a fittingly literal description of what a photograph physically is.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhàopiàn pāi de zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: Your photo came out really well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒujī lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhàopiàn.
examples.english: I have a lot of photos on my phone.

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的想法。
example.pinyin: Měige rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
example.fact: 每 almost always needs a measure word directly after it before a noun — 每个人 ("every person"), 每天 ("every day," where 天 itself already functions as its own measure word) — a bare "每人" without a classifier sounds noticeably clipped next to English's classifier-free "every person."

examples.hanzi: 每个星期六我都去游泳。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge xīngqīliù wǒ dōu qù yóuyǒng.
examples.english: I go swimming every Saturday.

examples.pinyin: Měi ge xuésheng dōu yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.english: Every student has a book.

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow.
又 here replaces 雚 (huān) in the traditional 歡, so it is only a stand-in; same shorthand in 观 and 劝.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go toward someone.
卬 (áng) is a loose sound clue for yíng; 卬 also in 仰 yǎng.

example.fact: 迎 (built on the walking radical 辶, picturing someone walking out to receive a guest) contributes 'to go out and meet, to greet,' while 欢 simply contributes 'joyful' — together 欢迎 reads almost literally as 'to joyfully go out and meet [someone].'

examples.pinyin: Huānyíng nǐ lái wǒ jiā wán.
examples.english: You're welcome to come over to my place.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā rèliè huānyíng xīn tóngxué.
examples.english: Everyone warmly welcomed the new classmate.

components.note: 攵 (tap) — the right part and radical, a hand with a stick, as in 收. Dictionary story: striking a beast, which takes courage, hence 勇敢 brave.
耳 (ear) — the left part, said to stand for a beast. Memory aid: dare to grab a beast by the ear.

example.pinyin: Nǐ gǎn yí gè rén qù ma?
example.english: Do you dare to go alone?
example.fact: 敢 is a modal verb placed directly before the verb, as in 敢说 (dare to say). It also appears in the polite stock phrase 我不敢当 ('I don't deserve such praise'), which is used to deflect compliments.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù gǎn yí ge rén shuìjiào.
examples.english: I don't dare to sleep alone.

examples.pinyin: Tā gǎn shuō zhēnhuà, wǒ hěn pèifú.
examples.english: He dares to tell the truth, and I admire that.

meanings: I, me (humble term used by men in public speech)

components.note: 儿 (person, legs) — with 口 mouth on top: the elder brother who speaks for the family. 兄 also in 况 kuàng.
弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.

example.fact: 兄弟 can narrow to mean specifically "younger brother," broaden to "brothers" in general, or — used self-referentially by men in informal speech — serve as a humble, matey stand-in for "I/me," a register-dependent range no single English gloss fully captures.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de qīn xiōngdì.
examples.english: He's my own brother.

examples.pinyin: Xiōngdì, jiè wǒ yì zhī bǐ, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Brother, can I borrow a pen?

components.note: 人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.fact: 从来 almost always pairs with a negative (从来不, 从来没) to mean "never" — used without negation, it flips to the opposite meaning, "always, all along" (从来如此, "it's always been this way"), so the sentence's polarity completely changes the word's English translation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cónglái méi qùguo Rìběn.
examples.english: I've never been to Japan.

examples.pinyin: Tā cónglái bù hē kāfēi.
examples.english: He never drinks coffee.
